name: Joe Pennell
role: Freighter; partner in Pennell & Roberts, Medora-Deadwood freight route promoter
bio: Joe "Doc" Pennell was a Medora freighter whose firm, Pennell & Roberts, joined the Marquis de Mores in early 1884 in pushing a freight and mail route from Medora to Deadwood and the Black Hills; the Marquis telegraphed asking him to organize post offices at ranches along the road. In February 1884 his firm lent its large room over the "Senate" for the stockmen's meeting. In April 1884 he and the Marquis set out from Medora at 4:30 a.m. hoping to cover the 185 miles to Deadwood in thirty-six hours; the trip took forty-eight. In late April he helped stake the route through the Bad Lands; in June the paper reported that Bob Roberts took out the first train ever to go over it, his and Pennell's. In July 1884 he helped decorate the hall for a ball and supper. From July 1884 the firm's mules did contract work on the Canadian Pacific, and by early 1885 the paper reported Pennell in the East, in charge of aqueduct work in New York for the Jones & Pennell outfit.
